results.title: Several Russian military aircraft enter S. Korea's air defense zone without notice: JCS
results.content: Several Russian military aircraft briefly entered South Korea's air defense identification zone (KADIZ) early Tuesday, prompting the Air Force to deploy fighter jets in response, Seoul's Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) said. The South Korean military detected the Russian aircraft before they entered the KADIZ and deployed fighter jets to prepare for any possible contingencies, the JCS said in a statement. The aircraft later exited the zone without violating South Korea's airspace, it added. The air defense zone is not territorial airspace but is delineated to call on foreign planes to identify themselves so as to prevent accidental clashes.

results.title: Korea University brings together global leaders at THE Innovation & Impact Summit
results.content: Seoul is the stage this week for a global conversation on turning university research into commercial and social value. The Times Higher Education (THE) Innovation & Impact Summit 2026, held at Korea University from Tuesday to Thursday, brings together leading figures from higher education, research and industry to explore how universities can deepen ties with businesses and investors, foster entrepreneurship and move academic breakthroughs from the lab to the market. Under the theme “Universities, industry and investors: Connecting research with commercialisation,” the summit examines the expanding role of universities in driving technological progress and economic growth.

results.title: As Google Maps improves in Korea, Naver, Kakao turn to ecosystems to defend turf
results.content: Naver and Kakao are doubling down on local business listings, user reviews and services linking place discovery to bookings and payments to defend their positions in Korea's mapping market as Google prepares to introduce walking and driving directions in the country early next year. The U.S. tech giant is moving closer to launching the features after making progress in securing permission to use high-precision map data overseas. A government committee on Friday reviewed Google’s compliance with security requirements attached to the conditional approval for exporting 1:5,000-scale map data. With Google a step closer to offering more advanced location-based services in Korea, the move poses a new challenge to domestic platforms that have built their mapping businesses around local information and services extending beyond navigation. results.title: Chonnam National University positions itself as key partner in Korea's 2nd semiconductor cluster
results.content: Chonnam National University (CNU) is stepping up efforts to become a globally recognized research university as plans move forward to establish the country’s second major semiconductor cluster in Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City. Under the government-led project, Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, two leading Korean semiconductor companies, plan to invest a combined 800 trillion won ($590 billion) to build four memory plants on the site of a former military airport. The region offers several advantages, including available production sites, an electricity self-sufficiency rate of 170 percent and the nation’s largest renewable energy infrastructure. The biggest remaining challenge, however, is securing the more than 23,000 skilled professionals needed to operate the four fabs. results.title: Jeonbuk National University accelerates AI-driven education transformation
results.content: Jeonbuk National University is advancing an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven transformation in education and research to improve students’ learning experiences and prepare them for future careers. Its student-centered approach combines academic flexibility, AI-powered learning support and programs linking classroom study with industry needs. The university’s efforts have been recognized in the Korean Standard-Service Quality Index survey conducted by the Korean Standards Association. In 2026, the university ranked first among regional national universities for the eighth consecutive year, marking its 11th first-place finish since it first received the recognition in 2012. results.content: Sungkyunkwan University has emerged as a globally recognized research-intensive institution, combining its six-century tradition of educating the nation’s leaders with cutting-edge innovation. results.content: Yeungnam University (YU) is gaining international recognition for transforming Korea’s “ Saemaul Undong,” or New Village Movement, into an academic discipline and a practical platform for global development cooperation, particularly across Africa. results.title: Tracing Gongneung-dong's changing landscape
results.content: The northeastern region of Seoul, particularly Nowon District, is often unanimously ranked on the bottom of foreign and domestic tourists' destination lists. Despite being one of the most densely populated districts north of the Han River, Nowon is sometimes jokingly referred to as “No One” or “No Jam.” Yet, it is an area with a lot of overlooked destinations and neighborhood charm. On any given day, visitors stepping out of Hwarangdae Station on Line 6 at the southern tip of Gongneung-dong are greeted by a cacophony of cars, buses and trucks inching along Hwarang-ro, a congested eight-lane road. Just above them is an elevated expressway with another four lanes of traffic noisily coming into and out of the capital. results.title: Zelensky says Russia receiving more ballistic missiles from N. Korea
results.content: KYIV, Ukraine — Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday that Russia was receiving "dozens of missiles per month" from North Korea, calling on European allies to send more weapons to respond "on equal terms" to the threat. "Russia is unfortunately receiving more ballistic missiles from North Korea. We are talking about dozens of missiles per month," Zelensky said. He added that "Europe has missiles that can deliver truly effective strikes" and asked allies to help in "countering Russian global banditry."

results.content: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump departed for Asia on Monday, turning his focus to economic deals and historic three-way nuclear talks with Russia and China as his administration adjusts to a new political reality in Washington. He said he may meet with Kim Jong Un while in China as the U.S. looks to reengage North Korea on its nuclear program. Ukraine’s losing Ukraine,” Trump told reporters at the White House on Monday morning before departing for his visit to Asia. “Russia is losing 25,000 soldiers in the month. results.title: Nat'l football team veteran says having temporary coach not ideal
results.content: DOHA — Veteran midfielder Hwang In-beom claimed Monday having a caretaker boss is far from ideal for the national team, saying he would like more stability on the bench. Hwang and South Korea will play their sixth and likely final match under temporary head coach Robert Moreno on Tuesday against Qatar in Doha. Moreno was hired in early September, about two months after Hong Myung-bo resigned in light of South Korea's group-stage elimination at the FIFA World Cup. Korea Football Association (KFA) President Chung Mong-gyu also stepped down, creating a leadership vacuum at the sport's national federation and its top national team. The KFA chose to sign Moreno on a six-match contract that takes him through Nov. 27, instead of rushing to hire a full-time coach while its presidency remained vacant. results.title: Trump says he may meet with Kim Jong-un while in China
results.content: WASHINGTON — In a surprise announcement, U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday he may meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un during his upcoming trip to China. "We may meet with Kim Jong-un also, so that'll be good," Trump told reporters from the White House before leaving for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China. Trump added Chinese President Xi Jinping might invite Kim to Shenzhen when the leaders gather. Trump is scheduled to meet with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC meeting. The planned trilateral meeting comes as Trump seeks a diplomatic solution to the war in Ukraine, while Washington and Beijing continue to navigate differences over trade, tariffs and other geopolitical issues.
